proof:
Source: Step (3b) of the parent proof of Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 — if Θ^{*n}(μ, x) ≥ t on A₁ ⊆ A₂ then t H^n(A₁) ≤ μ(A₂) — combined with outer regularity). Notation: ω := unitBallVolume n; B_ρ(y) := closedBall y ρ; H^n := μHE[n].

0. Compact exhaustion. If U = ℝ^N let K_p := closedBall 0 p; otherwise K_p := {x : |x| ≤ p and infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) ≥ 1/p} (p ≥ 1). Each K_p is closed and bounded, hence compact; K_p ⊆ U (points of ℝ^N ∖ U have infDist 0); K_p ⊆ {x : |x| < p + 1, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 1/(p + 1)} ⊆ interior K_{p+1} (the middle set is open); and ⋃_p K_p = U (for x ∈ U, infDist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) > 0 because ℝ^N ∖ U is closed and x ∉ ℝ^N ∖ U). Put W_p := interior K_{p+1}: open, K_p ⊆ W_p ⊆ U, μ(W_p) ≤ μ(K_{p+1}) < ∞.

1. Case n = 0. Let x ∈ Z. Choose r₀ > 0 with closedBall x r₀ ⊆ U; then μ(B_{r₀}(x)) < ∞ and ⋂_{ρ>0} B_ρ(x) = {x}, so by continuity from above μ(B_ρ(x)) → μ({x}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 as ρ ↓ 0. As ω = unitBallVolume 0 ∈ (0, ∞) and ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^0 = 1, densityRatio 0 μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x))/ω → 0, so the limsup is 0, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence Z = ∅ and H^0(Z) = 0. From now on n ≥ 1.

2. Decomposition. For p, m ≥ 1 let Z_{p,m} := {x ∈ Z ∩ K_p : limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ ≥ 1/m}. Every x ∈ Z lies in some K_p (Z ⊆ U), and its limsup is positive, hence ≥ 1/m for some m (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt). So Z = ⋃_{p,m} Z_{p,m}, and it suffices to show H^n(Z_{p,m}) = 0.

3. A small open neighbourhood. Fix p, m and ζ > 0. ν := μ.restrict W_p is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^N, hence outer regular (Mathlib Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure, MeasureTheory/Measure/Regular.lean:1072). ν(Z_{p,m}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0 < ζ, so outer regularity for arbitrary sets (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt, which applies to any set; equivalently pass through the measurable hull toMeasurable ν Z_{p,m}) gives an open O' ⊇ Z_{p,m} with ν(O') < ζ. Let O := O' ∩ W_p: O is open, Z_{p,m} ⊆ O (as Z_{p,m} ⊆ K_p ⊆ W_p) and μ(O) = ν(O') < ζ (Measure.restrict_apply).

4. Density comparison. For x ∈ Z_{p,m}, O is a neighbourhood of x, so O ∩ B_ρ(x) = B_ρ(x) for small ρ > 0. Simon's upper density SimonGMT Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity μ.toOuterMeasure (n : ℝ) O x = limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(O ∩ B_ρ(x))/(realUnitBallVolume n · ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n) (Chapter01/Densities.lean) therefore equals limsup_{ρ↓0} densityRatio n μ x ρ ≥ 1/m, because unitBallVolume n = volume(ball 0 1) = realUnitBallVolume n for n ≥ 1 (SimonGMT Chapter01.volume_euclidean_ball_eq with x = 0, r = 1, Chapter01/EuclideanHausdorffUpper.lean:71) and ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ) = ENNReal.ofReal(ρ)^n. By SimonGMT Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean:251; its hypothesis borel ℝ^N ≤ μ.toOuterMeasure.caratheodory holds because μ is a Borel measure) with A₁ := Z_{p,m}, A₂ := O and t := 1/m: (1/m) · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (Z_{p,m}) ≤ μ(O) < ζ.

5. Normalisation and conclusion. simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n = (simonHausdorffMeasureReal n).toOuterMeasure (SimonGMT Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure, Chapter01/Hausdorff.lean:445) and simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) = μHE[n] (SimonGMT Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Chapter02/AreaLiteral.lean:42). Hence H^n(Z_{p,m}) ≤ m ζ for every ζ > 0, so H^n(Z_{p,m}) = 0, and H^n(Z) = 0 by 2. (The modules Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison, Chapter01.EuclideanHausdorffUpper and Chapter02.AreaLiteral must be imported; their axioms are propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.) ∎

n = 0: positive limsup contradicts μ({x}) ≤ μ(Z) = 0, so Z = ∅.
Split Z into Z_{p,m} ⊆ K_p with upper density ≥ 1/m.
Outer regularity of the finite measure μ⌞W_p: open O ⊇ Z_{p,m} with μ(O) < ζ.
Simon 3.3 (SimonGMT mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity) gives (1/m)H^n(Z_{p,m}) ≤ μ(O) < ζ after normalisation.
